about.title: Hanford Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products cause injuries in ordinary Hanford settings — a kitchen tool that shatters, a power tool that malfunctions, a piece of furniture that collapses, a car part that fails on N 11th Avenue or 12th Avenue during the Friday afternoon rush. California generally applies strict liability to these cases, meaning an injured person doesn't have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product itself was defective and caused harm. That can include a flaw in the design, a mistake in manufacturing, or a missing or inadequate warning label. Because Hanford sits within Kings County's retail and agricultural supply chains, defective goods can pass through several hands — manufacturer, distributor, retailer — and more than one may share responsibility. If a product hurt you or someone you love here, keeping the item and any packaging can matter. Our team reviews these details and explains your options at no charge.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you may not need to prove the manufacturer was careless — just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be liable under California law, which means there may be more than one avenue to pursue in your claim.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving Evidence
items.desc: We can advise you early on to preserve the defective product itself, since it's often central evidence in a strict liability claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability law often relies on strict liability, meaning you typically need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury, not that anyone acted carelessly. We can walk you through how this applies to your specific situation.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep the product, its packaging, and any receipts or manuals in the same condition as after the incident. This evidence is often central to a strict liability claim, and we can advise on proper handling and storage.

items.question: I was hurt by a defective product near N 10th Avenue in Hanford — does location matter?
items.answer: The location itself doesn't change California product liability law, but local details like where you bought the product or where the injury occurred can help us gather records and reconstruct what happened. Hanford's retail corridors along N 10th and N 11th Avenues are simply useful reference points for documenting your case.

items.question: Is there a cost to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our service is free, and we generally work on contingency, meaning we're paid only if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to explore your options.
